# 11. Fusion and World Model

Each O-CPS participant maintains a World Model: its current estimate of the set of objects in its relevance horizon, fused from its own sensors and from received PerceptionSummary messages. Fusion is the process by which incoming tracks are merged with existing tracks or instantiated as new tracks.

## 11.1 Fusion Inputs

The fusion engine consumes:

- Local sensor tracks, in the implementation-specific format of the vehicle’s perception stack.
- Received PerceptionSummary messages, after signature verification and freshness check.
- Received Intent messages from the same senders, used to prime the motion model for near-term predictions.
- Current trust weights for each sender (§12.3).

## 11.2 Fusion Rules

A conforming fusion engine MUST observe the following rules:

- Local sensor tracks at HIGH or VERY_HIGH confidence always dominate over cooperative tracks for the same physical object. A peer message MUST NOT override a confident local detection.
- A cooperative track with no local corroboration MAY be added to the World Model, but MUST be flagged as cooperative-only and MUST NOT be used as sole input to automated longitudinal or lateral control.
- When multiple senders report the same physical object, the fused track’s state is a trust-weighted average of the reported states; the fused confidence is not higher than the maximum reported confidence, unless the sources are independent (different vendors, different sensor modalities), in which case the fused confidence MAY be one step higher.
- Stale tracks (no update within the relevant message-class lifetime plus a 50 ms grace window) MUST be aged out.
- A track whose reported position or velocity is physically implausible given its prior track state MUST be rejected and MUST trigger a misbehavior detector (§9.3).

## 11.3 Trust Weights

The contribution of a sender to the fused track is scaled by a trust weight in the range [0, 1]. The weight is computed as:

```text
w = w_cert * w_attest * w_history * w_conf

where
  w_cert    = 1.0 if certificate is valid and not on CRL, else 0
  w_attest  = 1.0 if attestation is current and fingerprints known-good
            = 0.5 if attestation is absent but cert is valid (Class A)
            = 0.2 if attestation is stale
            = 0.0 if attestation fingerprints are on the revocation list
  w_history = a rolling average in [0, 1] of the sender's agreement
              with consensus and with local sensors over the past 5 min
              (clamped >= 0.1 to allow recovery from transient faults)
  w_conf    = the sender's self-reported confidence, normalized to [0, 1]
```

Any weight of zero in any factor produces a zero total weight and excludes the sender from fusion for that message. Implementations MAY add further factors; MUST NOT remove any of the above.

## 11.4 Advisory Threshold

A fused track MAY influence driver-visible advisories or ADAS inputs only if its effective trust weight (maximum across contributing sources) is at least 0.5 AND at least one contribution is from a local sensor OR from an attested cooperative source at HIGH confidence or better. Tracks below this threshold MAY be displayed to the driver as informational but MUST NOT gate control decisions.
